$comment: Canonical model for Programs. Not fetched at runtime (no JavaScript); programs.html mirrors these records as static HTML. All seven are the hub's real offerings.

fields.id: string (required, unique) — stable slug-style key, prefix 'prog-'.
fields.name: string (required) — display name of the program.
fields.icon: string (required) — key naming the hand-written inline SVG icon used for this program.
fields.tagline: string (required) — one-line positioning statement, max ~60 chars, used as the card subtitle.
fields.description: string (required) — two to three sentences of concrete detail.
fields.format: string (required) — how the program is delivered.
fields.duration: string (required) — typical length of one instance.
fields.capacity: string (required) — intake size per instance. 'Open' where there is no cap.
fields.entry_requirement: string (required) — what a member needs before joining.
fields.outcomes: array of string (required, 2-4 items) — what a participant leaves with.
fields.is_placeholder: boolean (required) — false for all seven programs; these are the hub's actual published offerings.

programs.name: Bootcamps
programs.description: Focused sprints that take a member from nothing to working code in one stack — embedded C, Python for data work, or web fundamentals. Each bootcamp is taught by a senior member or staff mentor and runs in the evenings so it does not collide with lectures. Participants close the bootcamp by building and defending a small working project rather than sitting a written test.
programs.entry_requirement: Open to all levels; no prior experience assumed for the introductory tracks
outcomes: A working project built and defended in front of peers
Working fluency in one stack
A place on the shortlist for the next incubation cohort

programs.name: Hackathons
programs.tagline: Build something real against the clock
programs.description: Time-boxed build sprints run against a problem brief drawn from campus life or the surrounding community. Teams of three to five have 48 hours to move from a blank repository to a prototype they can demonstrate. Work is judged by a mixed panel of departmental staff and visiting industry engineers, and the strongest teams are fast-tracked into incubation.
programs.entry_requirement: Teams of 3-5; at least one member who can build and ship the demo
outcomes: A demonstrable prototype and a public pitch
Feedback from an industry judging panel
Fast-track consideration for an incubation place

programs.name: Incubation Cohorts
programs.tagline: Structure for an idea that already works
programs.description: For teams that have validated an idea and now need structure to take it further. Across a full semester each team is given bench space in the hub, a technical mentor, and fortnightly milestone reviews that they must pass to stay in the cohort. Teams leave with a working prototype, documentation, and a defensible plan for what comes after the cohort.
programs.entry_requirement: A validated concept, a committed team, and a completed hub project or hackathon entry
outcomes: A working prototype and technical documentation
A milestone record and a post-cohort roadmap
A Demo Day slot in front of staff and industry guests

programs.name: Weekly Coding Sessions
programs.description: An open, drop-in evening that runs every week the university is in session. Members work through problem sets, pair on side projects, and get unblocked by whoever in the room has already solved that problem. There is no registration and no prerequisite beyond turning up — this is the easiest first contact a new member has with the hub.
programs.entry_requirement: None. Bring a laptop if you have one; machines are shared if you do not
outcomes: Consistent practice and a habit of shipping
Direct access to senior members and mentors
The usual route into bootcamps and project teams

programs.name: Research Clusters
programs.tagline: Standing groups on an open question
programs.description: Small standing groups that work alongside departmental academic staff on a defined research question, currently spanning computer vision, embedded systems, and networks. A cluster meets weekly, maintains a shared reading list, and is expected to produce something citable. Output is aimed at conference papers, strong final-year projects, and national competition entries.
programs.entry_requirement: 300 level and above, with a demonstrated interest in the cluster's area
outcomes: A conference paper or publishable technical report
A supervised final-year project topic
Competition-ready research work

programs.name: Mentorship Tracks
programs.description: Junior members are paired with senior students and with alumni now working in industry. Each pairing sets its own goals at the start of the semester, meets at least fortnightly, and is formally reviewed at the halfway point so that a pairing which is not working can be changed rather than quietly abandoned. Mentors are briefed and matched by focus area, not assigned at random.
programs.capacity: Matched to available mentors each semester
programs.entry_requirement: Active hub membership and a stated focus area to be matched on
outcomes: A semester of structured, goal-based guidance
An industry or senior-student contact beyond the hub
A reviewed record of progress against agreed goals

programs.name: SIWES Placement
programs.description: Practical support for the mandatory Students' Industrial Work Experience Scheme. The hub runs technical readiness sessions before placement season, helps members assemble a portfolio that shows real work rather than coursework, and connects them to partner firms who have taken hub members before. Members are also debriefed on return so the next intake gets better guidance.
programs.cadence: Annually, ahead of the SIWES window
programs.entry_requirement: Students entering their SIWES year, with at least one completed hub project
outcomes: A portfolio built on real, demonstrable project work
An introduction to a partner firm
A technical readiness review before the placement starts
